correctness.rationale: The exact radial upper barrier and axial variation-of-constants bound give all forward orbits a bounded domain. The source equation reduces to a planar flow with exactly three equilibria; a nonpositive divergence strictly negative on every open area rules out cycles and homoclinic loops, while the two sinks exclude remaining heteroclinic cycles. Poincare-Bendixson then yields convergence of every meridional orbit, and the exact angular coboundary gives circle phase. Measure recurrence forces every invariant probability onto the origin and the two rotations, whose ergodic laws are unique; the variational principle gives zero entropy on each compact forward-invariant restriction. The algebraic identities are checked in standalone verify.py. The critical general planar theorems are used under their standard finite-equilibrium, bounded-trajectory hypotheses.

value.rationale: The underlying construction distinguishes local Jacobian stability from global periodic attraction. Proving that the origin and two circles exhaust every ergodic invariant law is a motivated, natural complete classification of the global stationary dynamics and rules out all additional aperiodic stationary statistics and positive entropy on compact invariant subsystems. The explicit angular gauge supplies closed asymptotic phase on all circle basins. This goes beyond counting periodic solutions or checking an arbitrarily small finite invariant.
